The ball itself continues around the circle;
it does not move back and forth along that axis.
resolvedSectionBreaks.after:
We can make this projection visible as a shadow.
Fix a ball to a disk that rotates uniformly, and shine parallel light toward it in a direction parallel to the disk's plane.
Place a screen perpendicular to the light's direction to receive the ball's shadow (Figure $10$).

resolvedSectionBreaks.before:
The ball moves around a circle.
We observe its projection, not a new straight-line motion of the ball itself.
resolvedSectionBreaks.after:
Hang a weight from a spring where the same parallel light can reach it.
First place the weight at equilibrium and adjust its suspension so that its shadow is at the same height as the disk center's shadow.
We can then compare their upward and downward displacements from their respective equilibrium positions.
